label: prf:bring-cone-reeb-quaternionic-twist
title: Proof of the Reeb quaternionic twist
html:
Proof. Proof of the Reeb quaternionic twist

Proof. The three operators are right-multiplications, so composing them multiplies on the right in the opposite order: for p \in \mathbb{H},

  (M_y \circ M_x)(p) \;=\; (p\,x)\,y \;=\; p\,(xy).

Hence

  [M_x, M_y](p)
  \;=\; p\,(xy) - p\,(yx)
  \;=\; p\,(xy - yx).

For distinct imaginary units the quaternion relations give xy = -yx and xy = x \cdot y in the cyclic sense \mathbf{i}\mathbf{j} = \mathbf{k}, \mathbf{j}\mathbf{k} = \mathbf{i}, \mathbf{k}\mathbf{i} = \mathbf{j}. Therefore xy - yx = 2(x \cdot y) and

  [M_x, M_y](p) \;=\; 2\,p\,(x \cdot y) \;=\; 2\,M_{x \cdot y}(p).

Taking (x,y) = (\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}), (\mathbf{j},\mathbf{k}), (\mathbf{k},\mathbf{i}) gives the three stated brackets. Right-multiplication rather than left is what produces the +2 rather than -2; the same computation with left multiplication yields the opposite sign.

Nothing in the argument uses an ordering, a radical, or any other archimedean construct — only the quaternion multiplication table — so the Lean statement is made over a generic commutative ring and specializes to \mathbb{H} = \mathrm{Quaternion}\,\mathbb{R} for the quaternionic-contact geometry. \blacksquare
